items.headline: Schedule your most used Copilot prompts
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot now allows users to schedule prompts to run automatically at regular intervals on hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly cadences. Users can create up to 10 scheduled prompts, with Copilot running them automatically and delivering results via email notification when ready, useful for routine tasks like summarizing information, drafting recurring emails, or creating weekly planning checklists.
items.levelshiftAngle: Our Microsoft practice delivers M365 Copilot implementations for 300+ enterprise clients. Scheduled prompts directly address a common adoption barrier we see: teams use Copilot reactively rather than embedding it into daily workflows. This feature becomes a capability conversation in our AI Discovery Workshops, showing manufacturing and financial services clients how to automate routine reporting, compliance summaries, and weekly team updates without manual triggers.

items.headline: Microsoft Build 2026 introduces GPU-acceleration directly into Fabric Data Warehouse
items.summary: Microsoft announced the first fully managed GPU-accelerated cloud data warehouse at Build 2026, delivering up to 7x faster performance at 64-user concurrency using the CoddSpeed engine. The system offloads SQL query operations like large aggregations, complex joins, and massive dataset scans from CPUs to NVIDIA GPUs with no infrastructure setup or query rewrites required. Early access opens July 2026, with one healthcare customer reporting 5x faster queries in production.

items.headline: KPMG pulls agentic AI report after hallucination claims surface on June 13
items.summary: KPMG removed its report 'Redefining excellence in the age of agentic AI' from all websites on June 13, 2026 after multiple organizations disputed the paper's claims about their AI deployments and GPTZero documented widespread citation problems. items.headline: EU AI Act high-risk deadline deferred from August 2026 to December 2027 via Digital Omnibus amendment
items.summary: The European Parliament approved the Digital Omnibus on AI on June 16, 2026, deferring high-risk AI system obligations from August 2, 2026 to December 2, 2027 (Annex III) and August 2, 2028 (Annex I). Transparency obligations under Article 50 still take effect August 2, 2026, while prohibited practices (since February 2025) and GPAI model rules (since August 2025) remain enforceable. The amendment also introduces a new Article 5 ban on nudifier and CSAM generation tools effective December 2, 2026.
